ai.description: Ghatixalus asterops is a medium-sized frog (40–50 mm) with a pale green back and dark brown mottling. It is distinguished by a bright, star-like golden iris and a distinct white stripe along the jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Ghatixalus asterops* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid golden-yellow iris with a distinct horizontal pupil, which contrasts sharply with the eyes of other species.
ai.habitat: *Ghatixalus asterops* inhabits evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high altitudes ranging from 800 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ghat tree frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of its high-altitude rainforest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ghatixalus asterops* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 50–100 eggs in gelatinous masses attached to vegetation overhanging forest streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ghat Tree Frog (*Ghatixalus asterops*) is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in high-elevation forests across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The *Ghatixalus asterops* emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard echoing from vegetation near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
